intro.title: JWT Storage & Decode in React
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that securely stores a JSON Web Token (JWT) in the browser and decodes it to display user information. You will learn the core concept of managing authentication state by storing the token in localStorage and extracting data from it. The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript for building the UI, the jwt-decode library for parsing the token, and the browser's localStorage API for persistent storage. By the end, you'll have a functional component that can save a token, retrieve it, and show the decoded user details like username or email in a simple interface.
intro.usecase: JWT storage and decoding is essential for user authentication in modern web applications. When users log into platforms like banking dashboards, e-commerce sites, or project management tools, their session data is stored as JWT tokens. Developers need to securely store these tokens in localStorage or cookies and decode them to display user-specific information like profile names, permissions, or subscription status. This pattern ensures personalized experiences while maintaining security across page reloads and browser sessions.
